source.title: Generalizability vs. Counterfactual Explainability Trade-Off
source.authors: Fabiano Veglianti; Flavio Giorgi; Fabrizio Silvestri; Gabriele Tolomei

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It contains unresolved appendix references (“Appendix ??”) and apparent formatting or equation errors, but the empirical results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests a related generalization question using ε-valid counterfactual probability (ε-VCP) as a proxy for overfitting. It reports ε-VCP, margin, and training-accuracy trends, but does not test the listed claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: Results concern ε-VCP and training accuracy or average margin, not held-out test error. No result tests the listed claim versions as stated; dropout is compared by ε-VCP, with no test-error result.
record.test_reason: The study measures input-perturbation counterfactual probability, geometric margins, and training accuracy. It reports no held-out performance or train-test gaps. Its dropout comparison therefore does not test V6, and input-space margins do not test V7's magnitude-scaled weight sharpness. None of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they conclude that average ε-VCP increases with overfitting and propose it as a quantitative proxy, claiming a generalization–counterfactual explainability trade-off. Their empirical results measure training accuracy, margins, and ε-VCP rather than directly validating that proxy against held-out errors or generalization gaps.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates counterfactual probability around training points and relates it to training accuracy and margins; it does not reproduce the claim’s experiments on random-label memorization, test error, or the listed model and optimizer comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Dropout rate 0.5 reduces ε-VCP and makes its increase less steep on the two datasets; the effect is described as mitigation only.

fits_no_version.finding: On Water Potability, logistic regression and a two-hidden-layer MLP show increasing training accuracy and ε-VCP alongside decreasing average geometric margin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Average ε-VCP increases as average input-space margin decreases during training in these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On Water Potability and Air Quality, five-hidden-layer MLPs with dropout 0.5 have lower ε-VCP and a less steep increase than their unregularized counterparts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can reduce nearby prediction-changing perturbation probability in these MLP settings.

record.problems: No held-out test-error results are reported. ε-VCP is estimated using 1,000 random samples per training point with uniform perturbations, which the authors acknowledge may not reflect real-world data geometry. Numerical results in Figures 3 and 4 are not stated in the text. The appendix references for further experimental details are unresolved in the supplied text, and the monotonicity discussion in Appendix A.2 gives qualitative and empirical support rather than a complete interior proof.

Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including small-data, excessive-dropout, and augmentation conditions.

record.verdict_notes: The 80/20 train/test splits in Table 1 do not supply held-out results. All row states refer to assessability of the listed claim versions; cannot_determine does not dispute the reported proxy trends.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label held-out accuracy, and the named architectures and datasets.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and held-out test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and their test error.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons on held-out performance.
Large versus small batch effects on held-out performance.
Whether dropout changes held-out error, including the small-training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train-test gaps relative to other measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.size_stated: LogReg; polynomial basis expansion degree d = 6; augmented feature dimension n′ = 5,005
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average ε-VCP, average margin, and training accuracy over training epochs.
rows.measure: Average ε-VCP increased as average margin decreased while training accuracy improved.
rows.value: The paper states that training accuracy steadily improves, average margin decreases, and average ε-VCP increases.
rows.note: The text describes trends; numerical values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: The reported trends are supported by Section 5.2, but training accuracy, input-space margin, and ε-VCP cannot establish any listed version's effect.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average ε-VCP, estimated average margin, and training accuracy over training epochs.
rows.measure: Average ε-VCP increased as average margin decreased while training accuracy improved.
rows.value: The paper describes the same trend as for logistic regression.
rows.note: The text describes trends; numerical values are shown only in the figure. Margin is estimated for the MLP.
rows.check: The reported trends are supported, but do not measure held-out generalization or weight sharpness. Table 1 supports SGD for this experiment despite Section 5.1's general statement that MLPs use Adam.

rows.subject: vanilla MLP
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average ε-VCP across training epochs and compared it with a dropout-regularized MLP.
rows.measure: Average ε-VCP as a function of training accuracy.
rows.value: Vanilla MLPs consistently yield higher ε-VCP values than their regularized counterparts; ε-VCP increases alongside training accuracy.
rows.note: The text reports qualitative comparisons and trends; figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Higher ε-VCP without dropout is reported, but does not establish higher held-out error under V6.

rows.subject: MLP with dropout rate 0.5
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average ε-VCP across training epochs and compared it with a vanilla MLP.
rows.measure: Average ε-VCP as a function of training accuracy.
rows.value: Regularized MLPs exhibit a less steep increase in ε-VCP; their ε-VCP is consistently lower than the vanilla MLP’s.
rows.note: Authors say the effect is only mitigated, and dropout may not fully counteract overfitting. Figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Lower and less steeply increasing ε-VCP with dropout is reported. Calling this partial confuses mitigation of a proxy with an incompletely observed reduction in held-out error.
